headline: Recommended a manufactured home park code amendment and approved land development permits for three projects.
summary: The board approved minutes and findings from a prior meeting, then voted to recommend a Land Development Code amendment on manufactured home parks to City Council. It also approved land development permits for 557 Stillwater Avenue, 200 & 210 State Street, and Milford Street Extension, each with conditions. The board also discussed attendance by its Associate Member but took no formal action on that topic.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the June 16, 2026 meeting.
Adopted the Findings & Decision for 205 Corporate Drive.
Recommended to City Council that the ordinance amending Land Development Code §165-121 for manufactured home parks ought to pass.
Found the 557 Stillwater Avenue application complete as a Planned Group Development.
Granted the Land Development Permit for 557 Stillwater Avenue with a condition on signage for a fourth building.
Found the 200 & 210 State Street application complete as a Minor Subdivision.
Granted the Land Development Permit for 200 & 210 State Street with a condition on an affordable housing agreement.
Found the Milford Street Extension application complete as a Major Site Development and Minor Subdivision.
Granted the Land Development Permit for Milford Street Extension with a condition on the water line meeting Bangor Water District standards.

Member Jonas moved that the Board recommend to City Council that the ordinance amending the Land Development Code, §165-121, to Add Flexibility for Manufactured Home Parks Existing as of January 1, 2026 ought to pass. Member Hobson moved that the Board finds that the application was deemed complete on July 7, 2026, the applicant paid all applicable fees, and the proposed project is a Planned Group Development. Seconded by Member Hobson. Roll call vote conducted – all in favor, none opposed. Motion passed.

NEW BUSINESS 
1. Amending the Land Development C ode, § 165-121, to Add Flexibility for 
Manufactured Home Parks Existing as of January 1, 2026 
Chair Boucher introduced the agenda item.
Page 2  |  1 1  
 
City of Bangor Planning Division 
Planning Board Meeting Minutes – Tuesday, July 7, 2026 
Community and Economic Development Direct or Krieg presented on the proposed amendment, 
explaining it would create consistency for requirements between mobile home parks created prior to 1971 
and those created between 1971 and January 1, 2026, adding flexibility for newer mobile home parks. 
Chair Boucher asked the Board for any questions. 
Member Brush asked about the possibility of removing the date of January 1, 2026, from the amendment. 
Community and Economic Development Director Krieg responded that she is not sure whether that date 
was a purposeful inclusion, but there is a section for mobile home parks that follows the current state 
statute. 
Member Brush asked if the item should be tabled until there is time to consider the date inclusion. Chair 
Boucher clarified that Member Brush’s concern is repeating this process in 5 to 10 years. Boucher asked 
if there is a requirement to include a date for le gal or regulatory reasons – Community and Economic 
Development Director Krieg responded that the date was chosen to capture the mobile home parks 
created prior to January 1 of this year.  
Chair Boucher asked if any Board Members agree wi th Member Brush to consider tabling the item. 
Member Huhn responded he does not see a downside of including the date, so he would prefer not to 
delay a vote. Community and Economic Development  Director Krieg added that there is a pending 
application awaiting the amendment’s approval to move forward in order to create improvements at their 
mobile home park. Krieg noted there is a section of mobile home parks that were completed after 1971 
but were not captured in the newer requirements. Chair Boucher agreed with Member Huhn. 
Chair Boucher asked the Board for additional comments. Member Hobson shared he is comfortable 
moving the amendment forward as read. 
Member Brush asked that if the date were to be removed, what the affect would be on the pending 
application. Community and Economic Development Director Krieg discussed that the amendment 
process would restart, with another first reading at Council, advertising a public hearing, and hosting a 
public hearing, so the primary affect is time. Member Jonas asked if that would add a couple months to 
the process – Krieg responded six weeks. 
Chair Boucher opened public comment. 
Ronnie Pinkham, former President of Cedar Falls M obile Home Park Cooperative, expressed concerns 
surrounding the word flexibility. Pinkham discussed t hat lot lines on site maps should have diameters, 
sharing that in the mobile home park, residents are attacking other residents over lot lines that are not 
yet approved. Pinkham shared concerns surrounding site maps lacking exact dimensions of lot lines or 
setbacks. Pinkham believes flexibility is too broad a term, and more guidelines are needed. 
Community and Economic Development Director Krieg responded that the public comment relates more 
closely to a pending application that staff is reviewing for an expansion at a mobile home park, rather
Page 3  |  1 1  
 
City of Bangor Planning Division 
Planning Board Meeting Minutes – Tuesday, July 7, 2026 
than the amendment itself. Krieg clarified that dimens ions would still be required with this change, and 
staff has not completed a review of the pending application until the amendment is approved.  
Chair Boucher clarified that the amendment is a standardization effort, and that it would not remove 
requirements to have lot lines – Community and Economic Development Director Krieg confirmed that it 
is already required. 
Chair Boucher closed public comment. 
Member Jonas moved that the Board recommend to City Council that the ordinance amending the Land 
Development Code, §165-121, to Add Flexibility for Manufactured Home Parks Existing as of January 1, 
2026 ought to pass. Seconded by Member Hobson. Roll call vote conducted – all in favor, none opposed. 
Motion passed.

OTHER BUSINESS 
1. Follow-Up/Thoughts on Land Use Plan Updates 
Chair Boucher introduced the agenda item. 
Community and Economic Development Director Krieg shared that staff continues to work on internal reviews. 
2. Additional Discussion 
Chair Boucher asked the Board for any further discussion. 
Member Whitford discussed the possibility of requesting that City Council remove the Board’s Associate 
Member due to excessive absences. Member Huhn commented that while he believes the Associate Member 
should be present to listen to the material and gain familiarity with ongoing projects, the rules do not require the 
Associate Member to attend. Chair Boucher discussed reviewing the bylaws to examine how attendance is 
stated, as he does not believe it is a requirement to attend unless the Associate Member is provided notice – 
Community and Economic Development Director Krieg confirmed there is not a requirement.  
Chair Boucher noted that there may be an opportunity in the future to update the bylaws, but in the 
immediate, there is an opportunity for outreach to the Associate Member to explore the possibility of 
increased attendance.  
Chair Boucher asked what the timeline is for the Board to review bylaws – Assistant City Solicitor Innis 
responded bylaw reviews can be completed at any point. 
Member Whitford shared that the Maine Municipal Association advises to create one or more Alternate 
or Associate Member positions to help with attendance problem. Whitford added that it is primarily a 
concern when a Member is unable to be present and the Chair must ask applicants if they are comfortable 
moving forward regardless. Member Huhn discussed that while it would be in the Associate Member’s 
best interest to be knowledgeable through meeting attendance, the Board does not have the same rules 
as the Maine Municipal Association. Chair Boucher added that their attendance would also provide 
assistance in the case of a conflict of interest. 
Chair Boucher discussed next steps to review bylaws . Assistant City Solicitor Innis added that City 
Council does have attendance requirements that could be mirrored for the Planning Board. Member Huhn 
discussed a requirement that Members must make contact in regards to a certain amount of absences. 
Huhn asked if the rules are able to be rewritten. Boucher requested an informal discussion prior to 
exploring bylaw changes. 
Member Hayes discussed the need for communication with Associate Member. Chair Boucher 
responded they may not understand that attendance is expected of them as it is not outlined as a 
requirement.
